name: Ivanti Vulnerabilities
desc: A command injection vulnerability in web components of Ivanti Connect Secure (9.x, 22.x) and Ivanti Policy Secure (9.x, 22.x) allows an authenticated administrator to send specially crafted requests and execute arbitrary commands on the appliance. This flow describes an unnamed organization that is a Volexity customer.

acts.d: The adversary uses a chain of two 0-day exploits.

acts.n: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
acts.d: The adversary wiped logs on the ICS appliance.
The adversary disabled logging on the ICS appliance.
The adversary downloads ICS appliance configuration files.

The adversary installs a backdoor in a legitimate file that is part of the ICS appliance image. This action requires several steps to remount the filesystem and ultimately hide the implant in compcheckresult.cgi.
The adversary inserts a backdoor into a legitimate JavaScript file used by the SSL VPN login form.
The adversary connects outbound to an IP geolocation service.
The adversary inserts a backdoor into a legitimate Python file called visits.py.
The adversary collects plaintext credentials from SSL VPN logins.
The adversary uses stolen credentials to access servers on the internal network over RDP.
The adversary establishes an SSH tunnel / SOCKS proxy through Cyberoam appliance back to their C2 infrastructure.
The adversary dumps LSASS memory to obtain additional domain credentials and uses those for further lateral movement over RDP.
The adversary accessed credentials used by a backup system called Veeam.
The adversary extracts NTDS.DIT from the hard disk image.
The adversary compresses the NTDS.DIT file.
The adversary installs several variants of web shells on multiple servers.
The adversary uses stolen credentials to access servers on the internal network over SSH.
The adversary uses stolen credentials to access servers on the internal network over SMB.
